title: Smoked Tri-Tip Roast
shortDescription: Santa Maria-style tri-tip with garlic herb crust for ten
subtitle: Santa Maria-style tri-tip with garlic herb crust for ten
description: Tri-tip roasts are rubbed with garlic, herbs, and pepper, smoked to medium-rare, then seared over high heat for a crisp crust. Slice thin against the grain and serve with chimichurri and grilled bread.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Tri-Tip Roast in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use fresh parsley, red wine vinegar as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season the tri-tip
steps.instruction: Pat roasts dry, rub with olive oil, then coat generously with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and oregano. Rest at room temperature 30 minutes while the smoker preheats.

steps.title: Smoke to medium-rare
steps.instruction: Heat smoker to 225°F. Smoke roasts until internal temperature reaches 120°F in the thickest part, about 45–60 minutes depending on size. Target oven/smoker temperature: 225°F.

steps.title: Sear the crust
steps.instruction: Transfer roasts to direct high heat or a preheated cast-iron pan and sear 2–3 minutes per side until a deep crust forms. Pull when internal temp hits 130°F for medium-rare. Target oven/smoker temperature: 500°F.

steps.title: Rest before slicing
steps.instruction: Rest roasts tented in foil 15 minutes so juices redistribute. Internal temp will climb to about 135°F—do not skip rest or slices will bleed on the board.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Smoked Tri-Tip Roast onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.instruction: Slice thin against the grain on a bias. Fan slices on a platter with chimichurri pooled alongside and grilled bread for soaking up juices.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Smoked Tri-Tip Roast — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: 130°F pull gives medium-rare after rest—push to 140°F only if the crew prefers no pink.
Freeze roasts 20 minutes before slicing if you need cleaner, thinner slices for sandwiches.
Save drippings and whisk into chimichurri for an extra beefy sauce without extra work.
tonightSpread: Sliced tri-tip with chimichurri, grilled bread, and a simple tomato-cucumber salad.
Roasted fingerling potatoes tossed in garlic oil for a classic Santa Maria-style plate.
leftovers: Layer cold slices into steak sandwiches with horseradish mayo and arugula.
Dice and toss into a hearty beef barley soup for next-day comfort food.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tri-tip delivers steak-house vibes at BBQ-night cost. The cook timeline fits a shift better than brisket, and thin slices feed a line fast with minimal waste.
mealPrepNotes: Trim silver skin the night before and apply dry rub so flavor penetrates. Chimichurri can be blended ahead and held refrigerated. Rest roasts fully before slicing—rushing ruins the presentation.
